cards.body:
## Summary
The client holds two independent hand copies of Rust's `MandatePayload::validate()` (the editor's `ruleProblems` and the mock's `mockValidate`) plus a third copy of the clause names and numbers in `words.ts`. They have already drifted: the mock knows nothing about clause 8, so the large scale world ships a rule the real wallet refuses and a test certifies it as valid. Fold them into one module, `lib/mandateRules.ts`, and pin it to Rust's own reason literals with a source-reading parity test.

## Description
`mandateRules.ts` owns: the clause registry (type, number, name, hint, required), `validateRules(payload) -> Refusal[]` returning every refusal in Rust's order with Rust's exact reason strings, and the reason-to-words table. `ruleProblems` becomes an adapter (skip incomplete clauses, map reasons to words); `mockValidate` becomes `validateRules(p)[0] ?? null`; `words.ts` RULE_NAME/RULE_NUMBER and `mandateDraft` CLAUSE_KINDS/CLAUSE_NUMBER re-export the registry. The mock's `mandate_sign` starts refusing like `Runtime::sign_mandate`, and the scale world's M6 'every' rule is reshaped into a valid nine-clause rescue rule. The parity test follows the existing source-reading pattern (windows/approval/notices.test.ts, lib/contrast.test.ts): it reads crates/table-core/src/mandate.rs and fails the build when Rust gains a validate() reason or clause number the client does not know.

## Flow
- Add mandateRules.ts + parity test (red: mock lacks clause-8 reasons).
- Re-point ruleProblems, refusalWords, mockValidate, words.ts tables.
- Mock mandate_sign validates; fix scale.ts M6; scale.test stays as the oracle, now honest.

## Expected impact
The judge path and the director run on the mock (T7): today the mock can sign and replay rules the real wallet refuses, and the editor footer and the mock what-if can disagree on the same draft. After this, one rule decides both, and a Rust change to validate() turns the client build red instead of silently diverging. Removes ~120 duplicated lines.

## Evaluation
Claim: one validate mirror, derived from and checked against Rust's literals, removes the drift class.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (no module; mock returns null for the three clause-8 payloads; mock mandate_sign never validates; scale M6 invalid).
After: 8 of 8 (predicted)
Method: simulation - walked mockValidate (simulate.ts:61-105) against validate() (mandate.rs:262-466) for roles ['shop'] + lever, 4-lever list, EUR lever, and M6; walked backend.ts:940-950 for a rescue draft without lever; the gate rung is the builder's
Result: better
Gate: architecture (moves the rule into one module; mock behaviour tightens to match Rust, no product behaviour loosens)

cards.body:
## Summary
The mandate editor knows precisely why a draft can't be signed, then makes the owner repair it by hand, one problem at a time. Turn each problem into a fix the editor can apply, verified against the same check before it is offered.

## Description
A pure module `owner/repair.ts` maps the draft to `Repair[]` ({ label, clause, apply(d) -> d }). Candidates: add every missing required kind at once (emptyClause), add the fixes rule / switch to 'only your own subscribers' / make roles rescue-only for rescue drafts, add a price range for haggles and shop orders, move a band's end to the rules' end, drop a duplicate, and pick a deal kind the allowed roles can act on. A candidate is offered only if `ruleProblems` strictly drops after applying it, so the module never needs its own copy of the rules (no third mirror). `FixLine` replaces the footer's gold text with the problem plus a 'Fix: …' button and, when several are offered, 'Fix all'. Field errors (an empty amount) are not auto-filled: amounts stay the owner's call. The SignSheet's unreachable problems list is removed.

## Flow
- '+ New' -> footer: 'Can't be signed yet: Limit per deal is required · [Fix: add the 3 rules every set needs]' -> one click -> levers for the three new limits appear, the footer moves on to the empty amounts.
- Rescue draft -> '[Fix all]' adds the fixes rule and the subscribers rule in one step.

## Expected impact
The first-rules and new-rules flows lose the Add-a-rule popover loop (one popover per missing kind, three on every new draft) and the guesswork on rescue and haggle pairings. Nothing is signed by a fix; the owner still reviews and signs.

## Evaluation
Claim: every structural can't-sign problem the editor reports today has a verified one-click fix; field values stay manual.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (no repair module; footer is text only)
After: 8 of 8 (predicted)
Method: simulation - walked newDraft (mandateDraft.ts:99-108) through ruleProblems (:329-333 required loop), the rescue pairing (:320-328), the haggle band rule (:334-335) and role/kind fit (:339-345); the gate rung is the builder's
Result: better
Gate: none
